newsitem.title: CANADA: Beleaguered Canadian defense minister replaced.
newsitem.headline: Beleaguered Canadian defense minister replaced.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien replaced Defense Minister David Collenette on Friday after months of opposition criticism.
Chretien's office said in a statement that Collenette would be replaced by Human Resources Development Minister Douglas Young as part of a shuffle that removed Collenette from the cabinet.

The two main opposition parties, the Bloc Quebecois and the Reform Party, had demanded Collenette's resignation in connection with an alleged high-level cover-up of a 1992-93 Somalia peacekeeping mission during which Canadian soldiers tortured and killed several Somalis.
In particular, Collenette had stood behind Chief of Defence Staff General Jean Boyle even after Boyle admitted breaking the spirit of Canada's freedom of information laws.

Collenette told a news conference his resignation had nothing to do with Somalia. He said he had stepped down because he had breached guidelines by writing to the chairperson of Canada's Immigration and Refugee Board. He did not give details of the issue.
Minister of International Cooperation Pierre Pettigrew was named to replace Young, and the Liberal whip in the House of Commons, Don Boudria, replaces Pettigrew.
